articles.title_orig: Anthropic becomes most valuable AI firm in first-of-its kind IPO
articles.title_zh: Anthropic becomes most valuable AI firm in first-of-its kind IPO
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the public stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion.
The artificial intelligence (AI) company's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology.
Anthropic's shares flew past its allocation price of $83 per share , showing there is plenty of excitement around AI.
Yet the company, which is behind AI chatbot Claude, will remain under intense scrutiny in the months ahead to answer the key question surrounding AI: is it all worth it?
In just a few hours of trading, Anthropic's stock seemed to show that investors remain uncertain of where exactly AI is heading. The share price rose immediately to $111.5, sending the company's market value to almost $2 trillion, before falling by the end of the day, with shares hitting $97.
Some investors said Anthropic's debut seemed to be a success, as shares rose roughly 17% during the day, but the broader tech market did not perform as well.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index closed down nearly 2.3%. Stocks fell in the largest tech firms, including Google's parent company Alphabet (down 3%) and Amazon (down 3.9%).
The build-out happening around this era of AI is among the most expensive endeavours in the history of technology, with more than $1 trillion being spent in the last year alone by a handful of major tech companies.
The speed at which investment has grown has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble.
"Bubbles don't burst on the day of the largest deal," Richard Whittle, an economist with the University of Salford said. "They burst later, if the positive future becomes suspect."
While the basics of the technology have been around for decades, the more recent advent of more powerful computers and related components have allowed the processing of more data than ever.
The result has been AI chatbots that simulate human speech and operate more quickly tasks like software coding, digital image generation, and searching the internet.
It represents a new way of using computers that has led to the rapid rise of Anthropic, which started just five years ago and is best known as the maker of the popular AI chatbot Claude.
As the first purely AI company to go public, Anthropic will almost certainly see significant swings in price on the stock market going forward, according to Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot.
The "initial exuberance" will wear off, Barringer said, pointing to what happened with SpaceX earlier this year.
That company, led by Elon Musk, saw shares jump by about 10% on the first day of trading, taking the company to a record-breaking valuation of $2.2 trillion.
Within a month shares had fallen below their debut price, and have mostly fallen further since.
Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time.
But many such companies, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world.
With Anthropic, investors are not only looking at a notable tech company with a major valuation, and a potentially big future in business, but a company that is the first of its kind on the stock market.
"There's no obvious peer to compare it to," Neil Wilson, an investor strategist at Saxo UK, said.
So, as individual investors and even researchers and investors at large funds ask themselves if Anthropic is really worth $1.5 trillion, or even more, there will be few answers available.
"We'll have a stab at it," Wilson said. "I don't think anyone really knows."
A few things will likely impact the company's success on the stock market in the near-term.
One of those things is the prospect of new laws governing the use of AI tools. In the US, where Anthropic is based, Democrats will be in many more positions of power come 2027, and several politicians have already said they will be looking to ensure AI tools are safe and have some guardrails attached.
On Thursday, the same day Anthropic went public, a bipartisan group of lawmakers formed the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, which will work specifically on AI regulation and safety considerations.
A significant driver of this kind of scrutiny is Anthropic itself. Company executives, including co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei, have been outspoken in their purported fears that future AI tools will become so capable they will outsmart humans, to the point where extinction is possible.
Anthropic has always put itself forward in public as an AI company that takes the safety of its technology very seriously.
Daniela Amodei, Anthropic's president and sister of Dario Amodei, boasted on Thursday that the company "had an AI safety team before we launched our first product".
"AI carries real risks," she added.
Despite the company's claims that the technology it is building at a rapid pace could be dangerous, Anthropic has made one of the quickest trips from start-up to IPO in history.

articles.title_orig: U.N. Court Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
articles.title_zh: U.N. Court Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
articles.content_orig:
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the predominantly Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017.
The landmark judgement in The Hague on Thursday is the first time a state has been held responsible for genocide at the ICJ.
The case filed by Gambia in 2019 has been closely watched by governments, lawyers, rights groups and Rohingya communities for its implications for how states are judged under the 1948 Genocide Convention.
The court said Myanmar has an obligation to compensate the Rohingya for the violations ‌it committed, with the terms to be determined at a later date.
Here’s how key parties and world leaders reacted to the landmark verdict:
The National Unity Government, which includes remnants of former leader Aung San Suu Kyi’s National League for Democracy party, said it respects the authority of the International Court of Justice and its judgement.
It pledged to consider the court’s findings and orders, reaffirming its commitment to accountability and preventing further atrocities.
A US official told Al Jazeera that the United States was studying the ICJ’s ruling to assess its implications, while stressing the importance of preventing the court from being politicised.
“The proper interpretation of the Genocide Convention is of paramount importance, as is preventing politicization of the ICJ. We are studying the decision to fully assess its implications,” the official said.
“We express our support for the people of Burma and share the grave concerns over the continued abuses of human rights against Rohingya Muslims and members of other minority groups.”
The Gambia, which brought the case against Myanmar in November 2019 with the support of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, welcomed the ruling with “profound satisfaction”, calling it “a historic day for international justice”.
The government said the obligation to prevent and punish genocide is shared by all states party to the 1948 Genocide Convention and called on Myanmar to comply with the judgement “fully and without delay”.
Bangladesh has welcomed the ICJ’s ruling and urged Myanmar to implement it without delay, saying the decision could pave the way for the safe, voluntary and dignified return of Rohingya refugees.
In a statement reported by the state-run Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS) news agency, the Foreign Ministry said Myanmar was legally bound to comply with the judgement and reaffirmed that repatriation remained the only viable solution to the Rohingya crisis.
In a post shared on X, the OIC commended the ICJ’s judgement, saying it offered “redress for victims and [upholds] the principle of no impunity”.
Antonio Guterres described the ruling as a “demonstration of international justice” and a reaffirmation that impunity for “such horrific acts must not stand”.
He noted that it marked the first time the court had found a state responsible for committing genocide and called on Myanmar to comply with its decision.
The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said the ruling was an important step towards addressing the causes of Rohingya displacement and finding lasting solutions, including access to citizenship and the creation of conditions for their safe, voluntary and dignified return.
The agency said more than 1.3 million Rohingya refugees remained displaced across the region, most of them in Bangladesh, while more than 100,000 people remained internally displaced in Myanmar’s Rakhine State.
Volker Turk said the judgement “clearly concludes” that Myanmar is responsible for “one of the most egregious crimes known to humankind.”
In a post shared on X, he added that the Rohingya people’s “suffering is a stain” on humanity.
Ed Miliband said the United Kingdom ordered the expulsion of Myanmar’s defence attache and summoned the country’s charge d’affaires. He also called for an urgent UN Security Council session to discuss the ruling.
He said further measures would be announced in the coming days to ensure those responsible are held accountable.
Yanghee Lee called it a “deeply emotional day for all Rohingya people”, adding that “justice has been decided, but not yet delivered”.
Activist Nay San Lwin said justice for the Rohingya means the restoration of their citizenship, recognition of their identity and their safe and dignified return home.
He added that their struggle would continue until those demands are met.
A coalition of 219 Rohingya and other Myanmar civil society organisations welcomed the judgement and called on the international community to ensure its full implementation.
In a joint statement published by Justice For Myanmar, the groups demanded reparations, the restoration of Rohingya citizenship and the safe return of refugees. They also called for criminal accountability for Myanmar’s military leadership, including Min Aung Hlaing.
Activist Wai Wai Nu, executive director of Women’s Peace Network, said the ruling had shattered the military’s decades-long efforts to erase Rohingya identity, deny their existence and dismiss their suffering.
“By finding that Myanmar committed genocide, ordering a guarantee of non-repetition, and ordering restitution and compensation, the world’s highest court has permanently shattered that state-sponsored lie,” she said.
The human rights group said the ruling was a “historic and authoritative recognition of the atrocities committed against the Rohingya and a rare moment of justice for survivors, victims and their families”.
Maria Elena Vignoli welcomed the court’s decision, calling it a “long-awaited recognition of the suffering the Rohingya have endured from Myanmar’s military”.

articles.title_orig: Stocks plunge as investors take cover amid growing uncertainty
articles.title_zh: Stocks plunge as investors take cover amid growing uncertainty
articles.content_orig:
Shares of Japan's SoftBank Group plunged 16.16% on Friday, leading a broader sell-off in Asian technology stocks following the highly anticipated market debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic .
SoftBank is one of the biggest backers of OpenAI, Anthropic's rival, having invested a total of $64.6 billion in the ChatGPT maker.
The sharp decline underscores growing investor concerns over SoftBank's aggressive bets on artificial intelligence, particularly its exposure to OpenAI, as markets question whether massive investments in AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.
SoftBank's heavy exposure to OpenAI has made its shares particularly sensitive to shifts in sentiment toward the AI sector. The stock lost 30% in October and is down 31% so far this month.
If Friday's losses hold, it would be SoftBank's worst day in more than two years.
Japanese semiconductor stocks also tumbled, with Tokyo Electron falling 7.19%, Lasertec declining 6.75% and Renesas Electronics dropping 6.71%. That comes as AI darling Nvidia slid 2.9% overnight.
The sell-off extended to South Korea, where Nvidia suppliers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics dropped 6% and 4.7%, respectively. South Korea's benchmark Kospi also declined 3.66%.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% overnight following Anthropic's highly anticipated Wall Street debut.

articles.title_orig: Gap names new Athleta CEO, lowers full-year guidance
articles.title_zh: Gap names new Athleta CEO, lowers full-year guidance
articles.content_orig:
Gap Inc. on Thursday announced Ashley Kechter will be the next president and CEO of its Athleta brand, effective Dec. 14.
Kechter comes to Gap from activewear retailer Vuori, where she was global president and oversaw the brand's global business strategy, marketing and financials. She was previously global brand president of Fabletics and began her career at Gap before that.
"I'm excited to return to Gap Inc. and partner with [Gap CEO Richard Dickson] and the team to strengthen our connection with customers and shape the brand's next chapter," Kechter said in a statement.
The announcement comes after Lululemon poached former Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger to be its chief product officer last month.
"Clearly, we're disappointed with Athleta's performance, and we recognize there's a lot of work ahead," Dickson told CNBC. "We had been in rebuild mode, but now we're really in turnaround mode."
Dickson said the company is focused on getting back to its fundamentals: fabrications, feature, form, function and fit. Dickson added that Kechter will be conducting a "comprehensive review" of the brand to reposition Athleta for future success.
While the execution of its strategy has thus far "fallen short," Dickson said this new approach will allow Athleta to fully realize its potential.
Gap also reported mixed fiscal third-quarter earnings on Thursday and posted flat overall comparable sales. Wall Street had been expecting a comparable sales increase of 1.3%, according to StreetAccount.
Net sales grew 2%, though demand softened in October and early November due to warmer weather, the company said. Store sales increased 1%, while online sales increased 3%.
Gap also said it's recorded a $420 million adjustment to cost of goods sold and a $21 million adjustment to interest income from tariff refunds so far this year.
The company lowered its full-year net sales outlook to be "roughly flat," down from previous guidance of up between 1% and 1.5%. Gap is also now expecting adjusted earnings per share of between $2.29 and $2.34, down from an earlier expectation of between $2.35 and $2.45 per share.
Dickson said in an interview that much of the lowered guidance was due to warmer weather in the first two weeks of the quarter, but he said Gap is expecting "meaningful acceleration" in shopping ahead of the peak holiday season.
"We're monitoring the trends, and we're going to remain agile as we respond to the changing business trends," Dickson said.
Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
For the quarter, Gap reported net income of $311 million, or 86 cents per share, compared with $236 million, or 62 cents per share, the year prior. Sales rose slightly from $3.94 billion the year prior.
At Athleta, net sales were down 14% compared with last year, coming in at $220 million. Comparable sales for the banner sank 15%, which the company attributed to "limited traction" from efforts to modernize its merchandise and marketing.
The company's namesake brand saw 9% comparable sales growth for the quarter, with net sales of $1.1 billion, marking an 11% increase compared with last year. Dickson said it was the brand's 12th consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales.
"Gap is really firing on all cylinders, and the consistency of the brand is really giving us confidence in the brand's ability to continue its momentum," Dickson said.
The Old Navy banner saw flat comparable sales for the quarter and net sales of $2.3 billion, up 1% compared with last year. It's the first earnings report since the brand, which has been experiencing sluggish sales, named Michael Francis as its new CEO last quarter. Francis began his role at Old Navy on Nov. 2.
Banana Republic saw its net sales sink 3% compared with last year, which the company attributed to delayed demand for cold-weather categories and a women's fall assortment that fell flat. Wall Street had been expecting growth of 1.5%, according to StreetAccount.
Dickson said the brand has since introduced new products and seen demand "rebound" as cooler weather has set in across the country.
"We've been encouraged by the early customer response, and we should see sequential improvement in the fourth quarter," he said. "There's some work to do here, but with peak selling still ahead, I'm confident that the team is focused on the right areas and [will] ultimately position Banana well for growth."

articles.title_orig: Is Nvidia Stock a Once-in-a-Decade Buying Opportunity After Its Latest Earnings?
articles.title_zh: Is Nvidia Stock a Once-in-a-Decade Buying Opportunity After Its Latest Earnings?
articles.content_orig:
By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 19, 2026 at 4:15PM EST
10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›
The past week has been hard on Nvidia ( NVDA -3.30% ) . The semiconductor leader had to separate from its co-founder and now-former CEO, Jensen Huang, after he was embroiled in a scandal involving alleged extramarital affairs, including with a woman believed to be a Chinese intelligence asset. Colette Kress, who remains CFO, has stepped up as interim CEO, leading the company through its first quarterly update since Huang's departure.
And what an update it was. Nvidia once again crushed expectations, but that wasn't enough to jolt the stock, which remains down significantly since it reached a new all-time high in early October. Is Nvidia a generational buying opportunity at current levels?
Death, taxes, and Nvidia's financial results coming in above analysts' projections seem to be the only certain things these days. In the third quarter of its fiscal year 2027, which ended on Oct. 25, the company's revenue came in at $115.8 billion, up 103% compared to the year-ago period. Data center revenue grew 110% year over year to $107.6 billion.
Nvidia's non-GAAP gross margin was 74.9%, compared to the 73.5% reported in the prior-year quarter. The semiconductor specialist's non-GAAP operating income was $77.9 billion, rising 116% year over year, while its non-GAAP earnings per share were $2.68, up 111% year over year.
The fact that profits are growing faster than revenue is a strong sign for Nvidia, given the industry's increasing competitiveness. While some investors worry that competition from custom AI chips will erode the company's pricing power in the GPU ( graphics processing unit ) market, as hyperscalers and other corporations increasingly opt for these custom chips, it seems, at least, that this hasn't happened yet. Improving margins are a sign that Nvidia maintains strong pricing power.
Meanwhile, Nvidia's free cash flow for the period was $43.8 billion, rising 98% year over year. The company also posted excellent guidance. Nvidia expects $130 billion in revenue (at the midpoint) for its fourth quarter. That would represent a 91% year-over-year increase.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26
Of course, Nvidia's financial results and guidance were only part of the story. The market wants to know how the company's efforts to replace Huang are going. Nvidia said it isn't interested in bringing back Huang, despite many people, both inside and outside the company, calling for his reinstatement. And it is actively looking for a replacement, although nobody knows when Nvidia will find someone to step into the CEO role permanently. In my opinion, that's both good and bad.
It's bad because the longer this search drags on, the more uncertainty it could add to the company's prospects. But it's good because replacing a CEO as effective as Huang isn't an easy task, and the company's board is rightfully taking the time it needs to do so, or so it seems. In the meantime, several factors highlight just how massive an opportunity Nvidia could still tap into, even as it faces a more stringent regulatory environment.
During the recent U.S. midterm elections, voters elected many lawmakers and politicians across various states who had promised to be stricter on the AI industry . This may result in delayed permits and slower data center build-outs. However, Nvidia expects a great year ahead. The company raised its guidance for the fiscal year 2028, which covers most of the calendar year 2027.
The company now expects revenue to grow 75% in fiscal year 2028, up from its previous projection of 70% -- and that's after also raising its guidance for its current fiscal year. If we assume Nvidia's fourth-quarter revenue lands at the midpoint, it could generate $423.7 billion this fiscal year and $741.4 billion next year, based on its projected 75% growth rate.
So, given its current market cap of $3.8 trillion, Nvidia is trading at 5.1x estimated fiscal year 2028 revenue -- that's more than fair for a company growing as fast as it is, in my view. However, the CEO search does introduce some uncertainty. And we still have to account for the risk of margin erosion as industry competition intensifies. So, what's the verdict?
Nvidia looks like a buy at current levels, but it's hardly a once-in-a-decade buying opportunity. Still, investors who purchase the company's shares today could see strong returns over the medium term.

articles.title_orig: AMD Slides After Hunterbrook Shorts Stock, Cites Circular Deals
articles.title_zh: AMD Slides After Hunterbrook Shorts Stock, Cites Circular Deals
articles.content_orig:
Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the company "has its own China problem."
Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.
The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers."
CNBC did not independently verify this information.
Hunterbrook also said that new export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips."
The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.
"The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson said in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity."
Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "important" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.
AMD continued to slide after-hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

articles.title_orig: Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
articles.title_zh: Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
articles.content_orig:
Tax software maker Intuit said Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock. The deal is set to close in early 2027, according to a statement .
The sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses. Five years later, the software maker is unloading the email-marketing company for less than one-third of that price after Mailchimp became a drag on its overall revenue growth.
The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset. The company bought productivity software startup Airtable in September for 10% of what it was once worth.
The Bending Spoons portfolio also contains AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.
In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment . The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the company tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, said at a September company briefing.
Also on Thursday, Intuit announced stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The company reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue.
While Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million.
Management called for $22.88 to $23.12 in adjusted earnings per share for the 2027 fiscal year, with $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $23.62 in adjusted earnings per share on $23.43 billion in revenue. Intuit shares tumbled 15% in extended trading.
The company said Mailchimp should produce $1.256 billion to $1.266 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue, which would be down 1% to flat year over year. In August Aujla said Intuit anticipated Mailchimp's higher effective prices offsetting increased client churn. Mailchimp was founded in 2001. Rivals include Klaviyo , which went public in 2023.
Berkshire Hathaway invested $600 million in Bending Spoons when the acquirer went public in July, and in October Bending Spoons said Berkshire invested another $330 million .

articles.title_orig: Next year’s iPhone Pro redesign sounds like exactly what I’ve been wanting
articles.title_zh: Next year’s iPhone Pro redesign sounds like exactly what I’ve been wanting
articles.content_orig:
Apple is reportedly testing four iPhone 20 designs, including curved-glass versions with nearly invisible bezels. Hereâs what the leaks reveal about 2027.
Apple is reportedly testing four designs for its 20th-anniversary iPhone, including versions with curved glass and nearly invisible bezels, ahead of a possible 2027 launch. Image: AI-generated illustration.
Apple may be preparing four versions of its 20th-anniversary iPhone, but donât start saving up for four new models just yet.
According to a Nov. 18 report from 9to5Mac, leaker Ice Universe claims Apple is developing two versions with flat glass backs and two with glass curved along all four edges.
The curved designs are reportedly part of Appleâs three-year effort to create a nearly borderless iPhone, with bezels measuring approximately 1mm. However, the company has reportedly scaled back the more dramatic curves of its earlier prototypes.
With the iPhoneâs 20th anniversary approaching in 2027, the leak offers a glimpse into how Apple might be approaching its biggest smartphone redesign in years. The question is whether all four designs represent future products or competing prototypes.
Four anniversary iPhones might sound like an ambitious birthday celebration, but the latest leak doesnât necessarily point to a four-model launch.
According to Ice Universe, the reported designs fall into two categories:
As 9to5Mac notes , one possibility is that Apple is testing two versions each of its expected Pro and Pro Max models before choosing a final design.
That would align with earlier Bloomberg reporting pointing to two anniversary Pro devices rather than four.
Apple routinely evaluates competing prototypes before finalizing a product, weighing factors such as durability, usability, and manufacturing requirements.
In other words, four prototypes donât automatically mean four new iPhones are headed to Apple Stores.
The most interesting part of the leak isnât the number of designs. Itâs what Apple may be trying to achieve with the curved versions.
Ice Universe claims the glass curves around all four edges, creating the illusion of an almost borderless display when viewed directly from the front.
According to the leaker , the curved sections measure approximately 1mm wide, while 9to5Mac also reports bezels of roughly 1mm.
The design has reportedly undergone several revisions over three years, with Apple reducing the more pronounced curvature of earlier prototypes.
Curved glass can create a striking appearance, but it also raises practical questions about durability, accidental touches, screen protection, and repairability .
Those are considerations for a potential finished product, not documented problems with Appleâs rumored prototypes.
And despite talk of an all-glass iPhone, Apple may not be abandoning metal entirely.
According to Bloomberg , Apple previously abandoned a more ambitious glass-heavy concept after encountering manufacturing difficulties.
The revised anniversary design reportedly retains curved glass on the front and back, separated by a narrow metal band.
Appleâs rumored redesign has generated plenty of excitement, particularly around the possibility of an uninterrupted display.
But that dream may have to wait.
According to a Nov. 4 report from 9to5Mac , Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station claimed the anniversary Pro models would retain display openings associated with Dynamic Island.
That would leave Apple with an iPhone featuring extremely thin-looking borders but still-visible camera and sensor cutouts.
A nearly borderless screen, after all, isnât necessarily an uninterrupted one.
Another Nov. 16 leak reported by 9to5Mac suggested Apple could use glass construction similar to the iPhone Air, but with more pronounced curvature.
Together, the reports point toward a significant visual overhaul, although they do not establish what the final device will look like.
Appleâs anniversary models are expected to arrive in fall 2027, marking 20 years since the original iPhone debuted in 2007. According to Bloomberg, Apple has been developing two anniversary devices internally code-named V73 and V74.
The devices are reportedly intended to succeed the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, with similar screen sizes and a redesigned glass-heavy appearance.
The four-prototype claim doesnât necessarily contradict those plans. Apple could be evaluating alternative designs for the two expected products.
Hereâs where the rumors currently stand:
Apple has not confirmed the anniversary devices or their specifications.
For prospective buyers, the most interesting question isnât how many prototypes Apple has sitting in a laboratory. Itâs which design the company can turn into a reliable, mass-produced smartphone.
The flatter versions could offer a more conventional alternative if Apple decides against the curved-glass approach. They could also serve another purpose within its product development plans.
But whichever design wins, the finished iPhone will need to offer more than an impressive first impression.
A nearly invisible bezel may make for a striking product launch, but everyday value still depends on battery life, camera performance, durability, and repair costs.
A more complex glass design could also make protection and repairs important considerations, although thereâs no evidence yet that Appleâs rumored anniversary models will be less durable or more expensive to repair.
For buyers considering whether to upgrade in 2027, the sensible approach is to wait for confirmed specifications rather than make decisions based on prototype descriptions.
Apple may be preparing its biggest iPhone makeover in years. Whether it delivers a meaningful upgrade or simply a very expensive way to make the bezels disappear remains to be seen.
In other tech news, Appleâs $299 HomeView smart display has arrived with AI-powered Siri, FaceTime, and personalized smart-home controls, but early reviews raise concerns about Siriâs reliability, limited app support, and privacy on shared household screens.

Blending analytical rigor with engaging storytelling, she now works as an editor across technology and AI media.

articles.title_orig: Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance
articles.title_zh: Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
SHENZHEN, China — Donald Trump met Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at a villa in southern China, an unprecedented gathering of a U.S. president with Washington’s chief geopolitical rivals bent on undermining American power.
The meeting, conceived not by policymakers but by Trump and Putin themselves, had a fractured agenda, with each leader coming to the table with divergent interests and different stakes .
But the image of Trump standing alongside Putin and Xi — then sitting alone with the two of them, at a great round table in a cacophonous hall — was itself the culmination of a decade of his foreign policy thinking , a great-man theory of diplomacy that has broken with American tradition, elevating authoritarian leaders over democratic allies.
The U.S. president appeared subdued, thanking Xi and Putin before turning to the press.
“No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement and speech,” he said, arguing he had a “special responsibility” to maintain dialogue with adversarial world powers. “We are really making history.”
Unlike at Yalta, in 1945, when President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet Premier Josef Stalin famously gathered to shape the postwar order, the American leader was not at the center of these photographs. That place of honor belonged to Xi, the host, who presided over the gathering at a remote retreat outside the city.
It was a portrait of a nation asserting its place among the world’s superpowers — the very image Beijing had sought in agreeing to host the extraordinary gathering.
“History tells us that when great powers are at peace, the world is secure,” Xi said. “When great powers clash, the world is in chaos.”
The competing agendas could make the summit little more than a spectacle, yet still produce images that harken back to the famous Yalta conference of 1945.
It was not immediately clear when the meeting concluded, after roughly an hour and a half, whether the three leaders had reached any substantive understandings. They were expected to discuss arms control and the wars in Iran and Ukraine, among other matters.
An initial readout of the meeting first released by the Russian side listed four points of agreement, broadly committing to work to uphold international security, minimize nuclear risks, increase petroleum output and, most specifically,  overhaul the United Nations and the International Criminal Court, which it said “must not abuse their jurisdiction.”
The court has a warrant outstanding for Putin’s arrest.
Putin framed the trilateral meeting as one of equals, elevating a Russian Federation that has been economically and militarily devastated, and ostracized from the international community, over its war against Ukraine. Russian state media highlighted Xi’s decision to place Putin to his right throughout the summit as a gesture of honor.
“I am convinced that Russia, China and the United States, our peoples, are capable of making a significant contribution to strengthening security and stability in the world,” Putin said, “if they cooperate constructively as partners on the basis of mutual respect, equality and a balance of interests.”
The Russian leader appeared almost giddy throughout the day’s meetings, and upon departing Shenzhen for the airport, escorted personally by Xi to his car, was heard saying, “I don’t think anyone ever expected everything to go so well.”
“The trilateral summit was a giant gift to Putin. It put him on a stage where he does not belong,” Michael McFaul, a former U.S. ambassador to Russia now at the Hoover Institution at Stanford, told The Times. “The photo of that meeting will be seen throughout the world, making it look like Putin is a respected leader of a great power. What did Americans get in return? Nothing, absolutely nothing.”
The unusual summit comes just weeks after Trump suffered a generational rebuke in the midterm elections and as he remains bogged down in a war with Iran, which threatened to erupt in a new round of hostilities in the coming days.
Publicly, Trump framed the gathering as an effort to curb nuclear proliferation. Yet instead of advancing a trilateral nonproliferation agreement among the world’s three largest nuclear powers, Putin offered a message of defiance, sending nuclear-capable bombers to nearby Vietnam a day before the summit in a rare deployment. China, meanwhile, rebuffed calls to slow down its breakneck nuclear buildup currently dwarfed by America’s arsenal.
The Trump administration let the last remaining U.S. arms control agreement with Russia expire earlier this year.
“Despite the talk of denuclearization by the Trump administration, no staff members prepped the president to meaningfully discuss this topic with Putin or Xi, who are unwilling partners for restraints and guardrails,” said Jennifer Hong, senior director of the Institute for Indo-Pacific Security.
Instead, Trump’s focus seems to have turned to ensuring nonproliferation not among world powers, but in the Middle East — the main justification he has given for launching war against Tehran earlier this year.
“We’re not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon,” he said at the top of the meeting.
Putin had hoped the summit would secure space and time to continue executing his war against Ukraine — a prospect that Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky, took seriously as the meeting was about to begin.
“Big countries always think that they can make decisions about the future of all the world,” Zelensky told NBC News. “It’s a huge mistake.”
Sitting alongside Xi, Trump said the two of them were looking to “help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine” and “would like to see it ended.”
Few independent analysts believe Putin is interested in ending the war in its current state. But at the trilateral engagement, Trump suggested Zelensky was responsible for Moscow’s continued attempts at conquest. “Things are happening,” Trump said. “I think that he, and I hope the other side, would like to see an end to that war.”
The meetings were Trump’s first with Putin since the two held a summit last year in Alaska, a gathering that failed to produce a breakthrough in Trump’s attempts to bring an end to the deadliest conflict in Europe since World War II.
Trump met individually with both Putin and Xi ahead of the trilateral gathering, despite White House officials insisting before the trip that a direct meeting with Putin was not on the agenda.
“Who is he? He’s my friend,” Trump said, walking toward Putin with an outstretched hand.
“We have had a great relationship for many years. We’ve known each other for a long time,” Trump added. “And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start.”
A Russian diplomat attending the conference with Putin told reporters that Trump and Putin together are “committed to a peaceful resolution to the Ukrainian conflict, though the Europeans are clearly trying to stand in the way.”
European officials have been wary of the Shenzhen summit, warning against the future of Ukraine being negotiated without Ukrainians present. A Chinese official told The Times they would have been welcome to attend, but no invitation was formally extended.
Xi greeted Trump at the steps of Air Force One upon his arrival in Shenzhen on Wednesday evening, reciprocating the rare honor Trump extended to the Chinese leader at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington in September.
While Trump’s meetings with Xi were the primary purpose of his visit, the Chinese leader is also hosting a major international conference, gathering leaders from around the world for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, known as APEC.

articles.title_orig: Live updates: Russia shifts on Ukraine NATO pledges after Trump-Putin-Xi talks
articles.title_zh: Live updates: Russia shifts on Ukraine NATO pledges after Trump-Putin-Xi talks
articles.content_orig:
European leaders have said they are ready for negotiations with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, in a strong show of support for Kyiv.
"Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".
They were speaking at Berlin's summit of Ukraine's allies known as the Coalition of the Willing.
Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side". Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks.
Trump had earlier held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen , south-eastern China, with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping and later dialled into the Berlin summit from Air Force One.
In a lengthy press conference following his talks with Trump and Xi, Putin addressed the question of multilateral peace talks, saying the Americans were "insistently" asking Russia to allow the Europeans to take part.
Putin claimed Russia was not against the idea but said Moscow wanted to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks".
"That is why, through diplomatic channels, we have invited the Europeans to come to Moscow in order to determine their positions. And after that, we will decide in what format we will continue the dialogue with Ukraine."
But Putin also said that "every day" Russia heard that European leaders were talking about war coming in 2030. "But we are not planning to attack anyone... Is that normal? I do not think so," he said. Still, Putin added, Russia understood that "discussing issues linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans".
Jared Kushner told reporters that the US president had come away from Shenzhen believing that "peace is achievable".
Striking an upbeat note, Kushner said that the Russians were willing to trust the instinct of the US envoys "on our behalf" that the Europeans should be at the table and that Moscow was now "comfortable" with Ukraine having security guarantees based on the idea enshrined in Nato's Article Five that requires allies to come to a country's defence if it comes under attack.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who also was at the summit in Germany's capital, has long sought a guarantee equivalent to Nato's collective defence clause, and there has been little indication that Putin would accept that kind of condition.
Russia rejects outright the idea of Ukrainian membership of Nato, but reports say US negotiators have mulled the idea of giving Kyiv Article Five-style guarantees without being part of the Western defensive alliance if it agrees to painful territorial concessions.
Zelensky and the three European leaders – Merz, Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron – were not as upbeat as Kushner, and the Ukrainian president made clear that the Russian president had spurned every proposal so far: "Putin has always said no."
The German chancellor was equally sceptical, although he said with US involvement the chance of peace was increasing. Europe was willing to enter "serious discussions on European security" with Russia, he explained, "as long as it's matched with a serious discussion and only first a peace agreement with Ukraine".
"These talks have to begin, and we will accept if conditions are acceptable for Europe and Ukraine," said Merz.
He also said any attempts to divide Europe into spheres of influence run by major powers was unacceptable, amid concerns on the continent that this issue may have been on the agenda at the trilateral talks in Shenzhen.
"A 'Yalta format' will not bring peace," Merz said, referring to the post-World War Two agreement between the US, the USSR and Britain in 1945.
Meanwhile, Macron urged Ukraine's allies to do the "maximum" to deliver the much-needed air defence systems Kyiv needed to repel deadly Russian attacks.
The French leader also urged the allies to "reopen the question" of Ukraine's membership in Nato.
There have been mixed messages from Moscow on European participation to the talks. Last week, following a visit to Moscow, the US envoys, Steve Witkoff and Kushner, appeared certain that Europe would soon have a seat at the negotiating table.
But the Russians were more circumspect and this week Putin's aide Yury Ushakov said a "great deal" would have to be done before the format could be expanded, suggesting that several more rounds of discussions would have to be held before any four-sided talks could take place.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
While Russia has engaged with several rounds of talks over the last year, little in Moscow's rhetoric or actions suggests that the Kremlin is considering scaling down its war on Ukraine.
It continues to pound Kyiv's energy infrastructure to cripple it as winter takes hold, increasing numbers of civilian casualties are being recorded across the country, and Kremlin officials have not budged from Russia's demands for Ukrainian sovereign territory.
As delegations were meeting in China and Germany on Thursday, several buildings in Kyiv's historic centre came under attack from drones. One person was killed in a strike on a residential building in the Podilskyi neighbourhood, while the Dutch and Austrian embassies as well as Saint Volodymyr's Cathedral reported damage.
And Putin also vowed that Moscow's response to a Ukrainian strike on the Crimean Bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea would be "considerably more painful" than what Kyiv had achieved.
He also said he had discussed a "possible ceasefire in a number of areas" but had decided against it after the attack on the bridge.
Still, Putin claimed to be "interested" in ending the war and was ready to make compromises, while Ukraine and Europe were not.
"I assure you, we have no desire at all to continue this armed conflict," Putin said, despite the fact that Russia has in recent months intensified its attacks on Ukraine's critical infrastructure as cold winter approaches.
Kyiv and its European allies say that – in the absence of any major success on the vast front line – the Kremlin leader is seeking to break Ukrainian resistance by leaving millions of civilians without electricity and water supply.

articles.title_zh: Deals: Xbox Black Friday Sale 2026 Now Live, 2,000+ Games Discounted
articles.content_orig:
NBC Selected independently determines what we cover and recommend. When you click on or buy through our links, we earn a commission. Learn more .
Retailers started rolling out their early Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals this week, so I’m sure you’ve asked yourself: are these discounts actually worth it? I’ve covered the massive sales for over six years, and I can say with certainty that they offer some of the year’s lowest prices across categories. But it takes a little bit of work to find the absolute best deals, and you have to strategize beforehand to save the most money.
To help you make a Black Friday and Cyber Monday game plan, I put together this guide filled with tips and tricks I swear by. I also talked to experts to get their advice about what to buy, what to skip, how to find the top deals and whether shopping in-person versus online makes a difference anymore.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
If you have electronics on your wish list — or are buying a gift for someone who does — now is your time to buy. Tech sees some of the strongest discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, especially when it comes to devices like TVs , headphones and video game consoles , says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley , a shopping and savings strategist at Rakuten , an online and in-store cashback platform. As a baseline, Vipin Porwal , the founder and consumer savings expert at Smarty , an online shopping rewards app, expects at least 30 percent off in most cases, except for TVs and computers , which are usually in the 20 to 25 percent off range.
Black Friday and Cyber Monday video game bundles are particularly lucrative. It’s one of the only times a year I see brands like Nintendo , Xbox and PlayStation sell their most popular console, game and digital subscription for less than each item would cost if you bought them individually.
Toys is one of the most competitive categories during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, both in terms of discounts and demand. You usually get at least 30 percent off, says Porwal, and the most popular toys sell out quickly — I’m talking a couple of hours, maximum. Once you see prices drop, buy your must-haves immediately. Some of the hottest toys and collectibles to watch this season are the Beyblade X , Jellycats , KPop Demon Hunters toys , Lego Pokémon and SMART Play , NeeDohs , Pokémon Pikachu Puppetronic , Sesame Street Tickle Me Elmo Giggle Max and Toy Story 5 toys , according to Adobe .
Clothes and shoes typically get marked down by at least 20 to 25 percent during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, says Porwal. Many brands run sitewide sales, so their entire inventory is marked down, while department stores and big-box retailers put most of their stock on clearance to get rid of it before the new year.
Almost every small home and kitchen appliance you can think of gets discounted during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, including that Vitamix blender or Dyson vacuum you’re dreaming about. In addition to items you use year-round, keep an eye on seasonal appliances, like space heaters and snow blowers , as well as tableware , home decor and other essentials you’ll need to host guests during the holidays, says Gerstley.
Don’t forget to think beyond tangible products during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, says Mackenzie Shand, executive editor at RetailMeNot , a digital coupon, promo code and cashback platform. There are lots of deals on subscriptions, experiences and activities, too. “Many streaming services host Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, which can lower the cost of your entertainment bill for the entire year,” she says. “Meanwhile, if you have travel plans coming up, be on the lookout for deals on things like passes to zoos, aquariums and other recreation-type places in your area.” Fitness classes, gym memberships, beauty appointments, educational platforms and event tickets also often drop in price.
Additionally, while Travel Tuesday, on December 1 this year, is a dedicated day for travel deals, you’ll start seeing offers well before then. Hotels, resorts, tour groups, rental home and car booking companies, cruise lines and flight booking platforms are starting to roll out their sales now, making it the ideal time to plan a trip. You’ll see travel essentials on sale, too, like suitcases , toiletry bags and packing cubes .
Because retailers know Black Friday and Cyber Monday are prime times for holiday shopping, many discount gift cards for literally everything: stores across categories, restaurants, movie theatres, spas, streaming services, food delivery platforms, and more. “As long as you plan to gift or use this gift card, you are basically getting free money from these deals,” says Shand. There are also strong discounts on gift sets, like those that bundle beauty products, gourmet food and beverages, travel essentials and accessories. You buy these sets, wrap them and give them to your recipient rather than having to curate a selection yourself.
No category is totally off limits during Black Friday and Cyber Monday — if you do the work, you can find a worthwhile deal on almost anything since the majority of retailers participate in the biggest shopping events of the year. But if you’re trying to narrow down your list, here’s what experts recommend waiting on and when to buy it instead:
No, Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals aren’t worse than last year, but they’re not dramatically better either, says Claudia Townsend , a consumer behavior researcher and expert and marketing professor at the University of Miami. “Prices have risen, while discount percentages are likely to remain roughly the same as last year,” she says. “This means that a 25 percent discount, for example, will yield a higher final price if the item’s starting price is higher than it was a year ago.”
That said, Black Friday and Cyber Monday are still the biggest, highest-revenue days for retail of the year. Retailers want to draw customers in with deals, so most save their lowest prices for late November. But a discount isn’t a compelling enough reason alone for shoppers to spend anymore, says Shand — they’re being much more thoughtful about scoping out real deals to get the best overall value, not just the lowest price.
“The most common mistake is allowing in-the-moment sales and marketing cues define one’s shopping list,” says Townsend. “That’s how people end up “saving” 40 percent on items they never intended to buy. I recommend that consumers create a list with a budget and a target price for each item, and commit to purchasing only when a deal reaches that price.”
Some retailers let you make shopping lists in their apps or on their websites and, along with certain cashback extensions, let you set up notifications when items’ prices drop so you can start evaluating immediately. That means you don’t have to do any browsing that might lead to impulse purchases — you stay zeroed in on your list the entire time.
Free tools like CamelCamelCamel , Keepa and Honey show you a product’s price history, as do built-in features on some retailers’ websites. Use them to determine whether an item dropped in price from a steady baseline, making it a legitimate deal, or if it’s marked down from an inflated baseline.
Be sure to also use price-tracking tools to figure out what a specific product cost during Black Friday and Cyber Monday last year. That serves as a great comparison point, especially for early deals: If a product’s price dropped more during last year’s Black Friday to Cyber Monday period than the two weeks before it, you can expect a brand to follow the same pattern this year, giving you an idea about when you should finally add to cart and check out.
Overall, “if the deal price matches or beats the item’s lowest price over the past year, it’s likely a good deal,” says Townsend.

articles.title_orig: Costco sees panic buying surge after tech outages, report says
articles.title_zh: Costco sees panic buying surge after tech outages, report says
articles.content_orig:
Public anxiety over a string of technology failures is driving some Americans to plan for the worst.
Jittery shoppers are stocking up on generators, shelf-stable canned goods, bottled water and other disaster-planning supplies at retailers such as Costco and Walmart, according to businesses and Wall Street analysts.
What's usually perceived as fringe behavior is starting to spread into the mainstream, according to RBC Capital Markets retail analyst Steven Shemesh.
"We've seen some evidence of it happening across the consumer retail space," he told CBS News, citing recent concurrent tech outages affecting online banking platforms , the Federal Aviation Administration's air traffic control system and even the National Security Agency . "Right now, on the margins, people are preparing more than they have in the past."
"People want to be comfortable knowing that if we did have an outage for a couple of days, they'd have food in the house," Shemesh added.
Data from market research and analytics firm Circana show that purchases of common emergency-prep staples rose for the four weeks ending Nov. 1. Sales of water germicidal tablets, which remove contaminants from drinking water, surged 154% compared with the same period a year ago. Sales of disinfecting wipes rose 72%, while moist towelette sales increased 20%, according to data from RBC Capital Markets.
Shemesh said that Walmart, which reported its third-quarter earnings on Thursday, told RBC that it is seeing a spike in sales of doomsday staples such as soup, water and ready-to-eat foods.
"It's not enough to move the needle for a company that does $8 billion in sales per year, but they are seeing those kinds of behaviors play out," Shemesh said. "Things could need to escalate quite a bit for this to go from level one to level three, which would maybe start to move the needle for some companies."
Nik Modi, global consumer and retail research co-head at RBC Capital Markets, is also seeing signs of panic shopping by consumers.
"A convergence of government action and social media anxiety has pushed 'doomsday prepping' into mainstream consumer behavior over the past several months," Modi said in a research note this week.
He traces the shift in purchasing behavior to a Pentagon military readiness initiative in late September that was misinterpreted and amplified on social media as an impending "blackout."
Government officials have said the recent tech incidents are not connected and were not caused by cyberattacks.
"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday during a news conference in the Philippines.
Yet many consumers aren't taking any chances. Earlier this week, investment firm Mizuho Securities said that consumers flocked to Costco after tech vulnerabilities heightened concerns about the risk of a major cybersecurity incident.
"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at Costco," Mizuho analyst David Bellinger wrote in a report.
He added that shoppers are "pantry-loading" and also depleting the retailer's inventory of "high-ticket generators," which were sold out online as of Sunday night.
Tractor Supply, which sells a range of tools, clothing, and heating and cooling equipment, told CBS News that it has seen increased demand across "several preparedness-related categories." It's selling more generators, liquid storage tanks, propane and accessory tanks than it did during the same period last year.

articles.title_orig: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
articles.title_zh: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
articles.content_orig:
The subagency of the Commerce Department that regulates and enforces exports approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies including Alibaba and Tencent as of May 2026, according to documents released Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs Committee.
Some of those approvals, made by Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, included sales to companies designated by the Department of Defense as "Chinese Military Companies," according to the documents. From December through May, there had been 3.4 million requested sales of U.S. AI chips to China, the committee reported, citing those made by Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices .
"Over the past month, the administration's handling of chip export controls has put our national security and technology edge at risk. The Bureau of Industry and Security has failed to enforce the rules, and Congress must now conduct rigorous oversight of the administration's policies," Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said at a meeting of the panel Thursday at which members voted to release the documents.
Spokespersons for Nvidia and AMD said their companies comply with U.S. export control laws.
Nvidia argued it was following the Commerce Department regulations that were in effect at the time.
"The review and licensing process spanned more than half a year, with approvals subject to strict conditions and limited volumes. Despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China," Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo told CNBC.
On Tuesday, Nvidia reported $2.4 billion in quarterly revenue from H200 and related chip sales in China. In total, customers based in China and Hong Kong made up about 9.5% of all revenue.
"AMD complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations," AMD said through a spokesperson.
The approval of 879,000 AI chip is "not that many," Bernstein Senior Analyst Stacy Rasgon told CNBC, adding that this news is not surprising.
"It doesn't sound to me like they're approving everything they got willy nilly," Rasgon said of the Commerce Department. With 879,000 approvals out of 3.4 million requested AI chip sales, he added, "There was a process in place, and it sounds like they approved about one out of every four."
Despite a rapid succession of China export controls on AI chips that started under the Biden administration in 2022, Nvidia and AMD both re-engineered some chips to comply and be sold legally in China. And in December, Trump said Nvidia could ship H200s, its older generation Hopper chips, to "approved customers in China" if the U.S. got a 25% cut of sales.
The U.S. then licensed Nvidia H200 sales to Alibaba , Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese companies, although sales were limited because Beijing didn't approve large-scale imports, chip analyst Patrick Moorhead of Moor Insights & Strategy told CNBC last week.
H200 sales numbers remained low due to those restrictions on China's end. Nvidia said H200 shipments to China made up less than 1% of data center revenue for the quarter that ended in July.
"In the grand context of the size of this market and how much they're shipping, it's a rounding error. It's tiny," Rasgon told CNBC.
The committee cited the Export Control Reform Act as justification for releasing the data. The panel said the law allows it to declassify and release export data if it "determines that the withholding of the following information is contrary to the national interest."
The Commerce Department did not respond to a request for comment. The license requests released by the Foreign Affairs Committee include requests to sell to major firms including Bytedance, Tesla (Shanghai) and Baidu .
The release of documents comes in the wake of Jensen Huang 's resignation from the chip supplier Nvidia after news surfaced that he had several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy that led to concerns about Nvidia chips being diverted to China.
In the weeks since, Republicans and Democrats in Congress have called for legislation to be passed that would impose stricter export controls on the sale of advanced AI chips to China and other adversaries.
"The license information we are disclosing today will help inform the American public about how BIS has handled licenses for Nvidia H200 and equivalent AMD chips to China. The public has the right to know how these decisions were made," Meeks said.
Mast said two of the firms listed in Nvidia license applications to BIS —  Maginfra and New Matrix — are suspected "smuggling fronts." The New York Times reported in November that both companies had empty offices and had ties to companies under national security sanctions.
"Both are fake companies. If BIS approved the sale of these chips to these firms, obviously that is of tremendous concern to us — especially given that President Trump made clear last year that the sale of any AI chips to China will have very real national security conditions," Mast said at the Thursday meeting.
Maginfra and New Matrix did not reply to requests for comment.
Shares of AMD fell Thursday after the investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging the company "has its own China problem." The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers."
CNBC did not independently verify this information.
Fallout from the Huang scandal on Capitol Hill has intensified in the last week, as lawmakers question the degree to which the former head of Nvidia's relationship with the suspected Chinese spy could have jeopardized national security and American AI dominance.
Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the panels Dec. 2.
Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., announced on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had also agreed to testify.
Lutnick has come under fire over his relationship to Huang and for his failure to take action on Megaspeed , the Singaporean company where Alice Huang , with whom the former Nvidia CEO had an affair, was an executive until 2025. U.S. investigators suspect Megaspeed diverted Nvidia chips to China.
Amid that criticism, the Commerce Department on Monday issued an interim final rule to close a loophole that has allowed Chinese companies lease Nvidia's advancing computing power from data centers in third controls.
The rule was "written by and at the direction of" the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS said in a press release.
— Megan Cassella , Daren Fonda and Kif Leswing contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Iran regime's execution spree continues as twins face death penalty, decades in prison after alleged torture
articles.title_zh: Iran regime's execution spree continues as twins face death penalty, decades in prison after alleged torture
articles.content_orig:
A cousin of Taraneh and Romina Rahimi told Fox News Digital that the sisters were assigned the official they accused of torture and sexual assault as the judge hearing their complaint. Fox News Digital said it had not independently verified the allegations or reviewed court documents.
The sisters, now 21, were arrested after January anti-government demonstrations in Isfahan. According to the Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA), Taraneh was sentenced to death and an additional 11 years in prison, while Romina received a 36-year prison sentence. The sentences were issued in the Shohada Square case, which involved 16 defendants.
This is reported by Fox News .
Their cousin, Masoud Nourmohammadi, told Fox News Digital that the official had been involved in their interrogation and later presided over their complaint against the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). He said the complaint was dismissed by that official. Nourmohammadi said:
As soon as they walk in, they see the exact person who tortured them and sexually assaulted them is the judge
Nourmohammadi said one of the sisters’ attorneys had been arrested, another had withdrawn from the case, and the family had secured a new lawyer to appeal the criminal verdict. He also relayed a report from another inmate who was with the sisters in prison:
We just heard from another inmate who was with them in the same prison that the girls have been throwing up, vomiting blood in the night
He claimed Taraneh had previously been unable to walk after alleged torture and that both sisters were being denied necessary medical treatment.
A Nov. 16 report by Norway-based Iran Human Rights (IHRNGO) documented at least 121 protest-related death sentence cases following January’s demonstrations. The cases included six women and at least five people who were minors at the time of their alleged offenses. The organization said some sentences had since been overturned or referred for retrial. According to IHRNGO, 41 protesters had been executed since March 18: 39 in connection with January’s protests and two linked to the earlier Woman, Life, Freedom movement.
Despite the execution of more than one protester every week on average since March, the international response has failed to raise the political cost of these executions sufficiently to deter the Islamic Republic
IHRNGO Director Mahmood Amiry-Moghaddam made the statement as the U.N. General Assembly’s Third Committee adopted a resolution Wednesday condemning Tehran’s human rights record. Seventy-six countries voted in favor, 27 against and 64 abstained.
Explaining the U.S. vote, Ambassador Dan Negrea said Washington abstained because it believed the resolution did not go far enough in holding the Iranian government accountable and included language that distracted from its main purpose. He said the abstention did not signal a softening toward Tehran and accused the Iranian regime of torture, terror, public executions and beatings. Negrea also said it remained the world’s leading state sponsor of terrorism and that its repression extended beyond Iran’s borders. He said the U.N. had documented human rights violations and abuses and that responsibility belonged to the regime.
Iran’s U.N. mission rejected the resolution, accusing its sponsors of politicizing human rights and ignoring the consequences of sanctions and military conflict.
Nourmohammadi, who lives in Utah, said he had contacted congressional representatives seeking help but had received no response. He said Tehran uses executions to intimidate people considering further demonstrations, adding:
That's one of the reasons that the Islamic Republic is executing people, is just to create that fear
He said the family remained focused on challenging the sisters’ sentences and securing medical treatment for them.

Host Harris Faulkner covers the escalating war before analyzing the arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East. Retired Blackhawk helicopter pilot Lt. Col. Darin Gaub joins 'The Focus' to discuss these rising global conflicts and U.S. military positioning.
Ukraine's military said it struck "one of the largest oil refineries in southern Russia" in the lead-up to President Donald Trump's meeting Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump will meet one-on-one with Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, China, a U.S. official confirmed to Fox News on Wednesday.
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said explosions "rocked" Russia's Krasnodar Krai region last night and into this morning as Ukrainian forces "carried out air strikes against the Ilsky and Afipsky oil refineries, two key fuel suppliers in southern Russia."
"Explosions and smoke were reported in the vicinity of the Ilsky Oil Refinery. Storage tanks were hit," it added. "The Ilsky Oil Refinery is one of the largest oil refineries in southern Russia, with an annual processing capacity of approximately 6.6 million tons of crude oil. Its products are used, among other purposes, to meet the fuel requirements of the aggressor state's armed forces."
UKRAINE RELEASES VIDEO SHOWING DAMAGE TO PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE FOLLOWING 'UNPRECEDENTED OPERATION' IN CRIMEA
China's President Xi Jinping stands as President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin shake hands before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press via AP)
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said an oil processing unit at the Afipsky Oil Refinery was damaged.
"Located in southern Russia, they provide some of the shortest supply routes for delivering fuel to Russian forces deployed on the frontline," it also said about the two facilities. "Consequently, every fire at these facilities means less diesel and petrol for the Russian military, and fewer oil revenues for the Russian aggressor to purchase missiles and Shahed-type attack drones."
TRUMP ARRIVES IN CHINA FOR HIGH-STAKES TRILATERAL TALKS WITH XI, PUTIN DURING IRAN WAR
The strikes unfolded as Russia launched drone attacks Wednesday on a residential area in Odesa, Ukraine, killing multiple people, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
"A brutal and deliberate strike directly against people, against life itself. And further proof of what the Russians really want and how they truly regard diplomatic efforts," Zelenskyy wrote on X.
People stand on a street near damaged cars and residential buildings following Russian drone attacks in Odesa on Nov. 18, 2026, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Russian strikes on the historic center of Ukraine's southern city killed at least four people and wounded several others, local authorities said. (AFP via Getty Images)

articles.title_orig: China gives Japan PM frosty welcome at Apec amid fanfare for other leaders
articles.title_zh: China gives Japan PM frosty welcome at Apec amid fanfare for other leaders
articles.content_orig:
US president appeared to doze off while Chinese leader made speech, but White House insisted he was awake
Donald Trump was, again, accused of falling asleep during a televised event, this time during the speech of the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in China.
The US president appeared to close his eyes for roughly 10 seconds on Thursday. As his eyes closed, Trump’s head tilted downward, and his hands remained clasped in front of him.
Several prominent Trump critics on social media alleged that the US president was asleep, including Republicans Against Trump , California governor Gavin Newsom’s press office and conservative lawyer George Conway .
White House officials denied the allegations, claiming the 80-year-old US president was looking down at papers in front of him.
“Fake News! President Trump was looking at papers in front of him while the speaker made remarks. You can clearly see his eyes move back and forth,” Steven Cheung, the White House director of communications, wrote on X in response to a Newsweek article.
“This is why the people despise media so much. They constantly lie,” Cheung added.
Trump often faces accusations of falling asleep during televised events such as Oval Office press conferences, cabinet meetings and sporting events.
Occasionally, while listening to other people speak, the US president will close his eyes for several seconds, appearing as though he is falling asleep . Despite footage of the instances going viral, the White House and Trump allies have insisted the US president does not fall asleep during meetings.
Administration officials have excused Trump’s apparent drowsiness as blinking or an example of the president listening intently. They consistently claim Trump “doesn’t sleep”.
Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, testified to lawmakers earlier this year that he had “never seen” Trump fall asleep.
“On the contrary, the guy doesn’t sleep, which is a big problem because he calls me at two in the morning,” Rubio said in June.
Last year, JD Vance said that Trump hardly ever sleeps, even while traveling overnight.
“If we go on a 20-hour trip somewhere, he doesn’t sleep the entire time. And of course, if he’s not sleeping, if he’s working, he expects everybody else to be working too,” Vance told Fox News .
Trump became the oldest US president ever inaugurated when he was sworn in nearly two years ago. Despite his age, Trump often claims he is in near-perfect health , often bragging about his “perfect” cognitive test results and insisting he has a lot of energy.
